answer: Networks resist Sybil attacks by combining game-theoretic multi-agent auditing with topological cut verifications. Auditing agents monitor interaction graphs; any suspicious cluster attempting to isolate graph flow triggers a verification pulse. If a topological cut exposes colluding nodes, their bonded stake undergoes total slashing. Maliciously minting identities yields superlinear attacker cost, transforming the graph into a secure haven where honest interaction can thread between verified nodes.
